bull_bear.body: Funding via internal accruals + bank borrowing. Land: 2-3 own plots in Wada (advanced commercial talks, finalize by Jun/Jul) and SIPCOT long-lease in Chennai. New plant lead time ~15 months (±3). Backup: shift Chennai stud line to long-lease, expand bolt in-house — "will not miss any order."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Forex volatility (drove FY26 margin dip); reduced hedge ratio raises exposure.
- Commodity/gas-cost inflation with pass-through lag.
- Patent litigation on wedge-lock washers ongoing (next hearing June; no arguments yet).
- Land/capacity timing — only 1-2 yr runway after Phase 2 unless new land secured.
- Working-capital drag from Chennai ramp-up inventory.
- EU-India FTA benefit (3.7% duty → 0 from Jan-27) likely offset by CBAM.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and granular; detailed ramp/capacity roadmap; candid that land is "not yet closed" and margin dip is forex-driven, not structural. Constructive on demand visibility.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Bolts (not studs) are the real TAM unlock: studs ~US$1bn, bolts/nuts lift addressable to US$2.5bn; industrial bolt pull bigger than studs in many segments.
- Offshore-wind entry (Europe OEM) is a new addressable-market door, targeted ~10% of fastener sales in 2-3 yrs.
- No powder metallurgy — buys sheet/coil/wire/rod.
- Margin dip is non-cash forex, masking stable operating economics.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds fully accounted: INR 1,212.4 Mn received in the Monitoring Account, INR 873.4 Mn utilised for payment, FDs of INR 200.0 Mn (HDFC Bank) and INR 134.8 Mn (Yes Bank), interest earned INR 4.2 Mn, leaving INR 0.0 balance in the Monitoring Account.
- Loan repayment was the single largest use: INR 454.3 Mn earmarked and INR 454.3 Mn fully utilised; finance cost fell from INR 61 Mn (FY24) to INR 38 Mn (FY25) to INR 28 Mn (FY26).
- General Corporate Purposes remain largely undeployed: INR 277.4 Mn earmarked, only INR 11.4 Mn utilised, INR 266.1 Mn balance; total balance available across heads is INR 339.0 Mn.
- Net worth built from INR 1,045 Mn (FY24) to INR 2,563 Mn (FY25) to INR 2,925 Mn (FY26), while returns compressed post-IPO: ROE 26.14% / 15.02% / 13.34% and ROCE 21.14% / 14.95% / 13.94% over FY24-FY26 (ROE excludes exceptional items).
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026 reads Promoter 54.34%, DII 5.78%, FPI 1.30%, Public 38.58%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **DSS** ~49% FY26 — stable recurring base; includes gallock wedge-lock washers (added ~5 yrs ago, ~INR 1,500 cr global TAM vs ~INR 2,000 cr disc-spring TAM); competes mainly with European producers.
- **SFS** ~34%, +64% FY26, crossed INR 108 cr — fastest grower; studs (~US$1bn TAM) + new bolts/nuts (expands addressable to US$2.5bn global ~US$100bn total fastener market).
- **CSS** ~17% — steady; import-substitution opportunity.
- Margins broadly similar (17-19%) across all three groups.

business.body:
- Deck claims a 70% 'Domestic Renewal DSS Market Share', 30+ years of operations, 175+ customers and 800+ SKUs, describing the company as 'a renowned and preferred manufacturer of precision components in India'.
- Product families are Special Fastening Solutions (High Tensile Fasteners - Studs, Anchor Bolts, Cross Bolts, Hex Bolts, Nuts, Gallock Wedge Lock and Grip Lock Washers), Disc & Strip Springs (DSS) and Coil & Spiral Springs (CSS).
- Customer base is described as major OEMs, Tier-1 and Channel Partners across Renewable Energy, Industrials and Mobility; marquee clients named are GE Vernova, John Deere India Pvt Ltd, ABB and Siemens Energy.
- Exports to more than 25 countries with an office in Frankfurt, Germany; export revenues contributed 33.7% in Q1-FY27. Q1-FY27 geographical sales chart reads India 66%, Europe 25%, America 6%, ROW 3%.
- Certified to ISO 9001:2015 / 14001:2015 / 45001:2018 and IATF16949 / BIS quality standards.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] Order booking increased by ~40% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, which the deck describes as 'reflecting continued demand momentum'; no absolute order-book value is disclosed.
- [Growth track record] The snapshot slide claims Revenue CAGR 22%, EBITDA CAGR 28% and PAT CAGR 52% for 2022-26, though the deck's own financial tables only go back to FY24.
- [Investor relations] Investor relations is outsourced to Valorem Advisors, whose separate disclaimer states its directors and employees own no stock in the company.
- [Market data] As on 30 June 2026 the deck lists CMP INR 1,108.95, 52-week H/L INR 1,198.60 / 648.05, market capitalisation INR 14,212.52 Mn and shares outstanding 12.82 Mn.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA 16.51% vs ~17.1% FY25; ~1pp / INR 3.23 cr drop entirely a forex (non-cash forward-cover) loss, not mix/RM. RM is 100% pass-through; gas/process cost inflation being passed with a lag (price talks started April). Hedging policy changed: forward cover cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections (12-month horizon); US imports give natural hedge.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body:
- Q3 FY26 (call 06-Feb-2026): Chennai generated ~INR 11 cr in Q3; price agreements with 4 wind OEMs concluded; 9M revenue +32%-ish trajectory; SKUs ~750; DSS ~48% / SFS ~35% / CSS ~17%.
- Q4 FY26 (this call): SKUs grew to ~800; Chennai hit ~INR 5 cr/month run-rate, FY26 util ~35%; SFS crossed INR 108 cr (+64% FY); commenced bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India in Q4; entered offshore wind (Europe); Phase 2 capex started (done Jun-Jul → 120 cr p.a.); hedge cover cut 70%→40%; FY26 margin 16.51% (forex-driven dip); SAP S/4HANA + 1.8 MW solar initiated; FY27 Chennai guide ~INR 80 cr; new Wada/Chennai land near finalization with ~INR 50 cr FY27 capex.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- Company growth 20-25% revenue CAGR; wind 25-30% short term.
- EBITDA margin to normalize 17-19% by FY27-end (assuming no further forex/commodity volatility).
- Chennai: ~INR 80 cr revenue FY27 (~67-70% of 120 cr capacity); exit run-rate INR 9-10 cr/month.
- Export contribution to stay 35-40% of sales.
- Offshore wind ~10% of fastener sales in 2-3 yrs.
- Cash flow conversion to improve ~10% YoY.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No consolidated order-book figure given. Price agreements concluded with 4 wind-turbine OEMs for Chennai bolts; commenced high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India in Q4; entered offshore wind (Europe global OEM, FY26). Industrial bolt inquiries/orders frozen in gas turbine, railways, mining, construction & agri equipment.
outlook.title: Order book / visibility

outlook.body: ~10% new customers/yr + ~10-12% new parts (bolts/gallock/retractor springs) to existing customers + 5-7% organic = ~30% FY26 growth. Fasteners the fastest path on TAM expansion; bolts open industrial verticals (gas turbine, railways, mining, construction, agri).
outlook.title: Growth drivers

risks.note: IMF's World Economic Outlook (April 2026) flagged downside risks dominating the global outlook, including broader conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade tensions, elevated debt and financial market vulnerability — a macro backdrop the Company operates against.
WTO has highlighted that global trade remains exposed to trade policy uncertainty, tariffs, conflict-related disruptions and higher fuel costs, relevant given Gala's export exposure.
Gala's products depend on steel, alloy steel and other engineered materials; sharp movements in raw material prices can affect input costs, working capital and margins.
As a company serving export markets and importing certain inputs or equipment, Gala remains exposed to foreign exchange movement.
The springs and fasteners industry includes both domestic and global competitors; customers compare suppliers on cost, quality, delivery, technical capability, approvals and track record.
risks.risk: Competition from domestic and international players

risks.note: Gala's products are used in applications where failure can affect safety, equipment performance and customer operations, given their safety-critical end uses.

End-user industries such as hydrogen, EVs, railways, renewable energy and electrical equipment are evolving; component requirements may change over a 10-15 year horizon due to new designs, materials, standards and customer expectations.
